text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State-owned NNPC oil firm appeals against judgment of high court that it must insure its assets with state insurer NICON.
- Chief of Defence Staff Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar tells defence correspondents at New Year party that possibility of reprieve for coup convicts not foreclosed.
- Central Bank may soon lift embargo on licensing new banks, official sources say.
- Shell to spend 36 billion naira to improve its Forcados oil loading terminal, says a company executive.
- Minister of Commerce Rear Admiral Jubrila Ayinla tells news conference in northern Kaduna city that incidence of trade malpractices declined by 65 percent in 1996 from previous year.
- This year's fiscal budget is likely to be broadcast not later than Friday next week, says finance minister Anthony Ani.
- No efforts will be spared to apprehend culprits of recent bomb blasts in Nigeria, says Chief of Defence Staff Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar.
- Equitorial Guinea may enlist Nigeria's assistance in training its oil industry technicians, says that country's information minister in interview with The Guardian in Malabo.
- Unipetrol shares emerge the most expensive on Nigerian stock exchange at 58.90 naira on last day of trading in 1996.
- Sources say top leaders of northern Nigeria are against government decision to privatise major enterprises in 1997 but this is unlikely to stop programme.

- Lagos international trade fair complex where exhibitions are staged annually is to be sold to private sector operators and turned into shopping mall, says Commerce Minister Rear Admiral Jubrila Ayinla.
